# Sizing a power station for a fridge

**For a typical full-size fridge, aim for about 2,000 Wh with at least 1,300 W of surge output.** That covers a day and a half or more. A ~1,000 Wh unit covers most of a day if you keep the door shut.

## The three numbers

1. **Continuous watts.** A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, which almost any 1,000 W-class station handles ([BlackBoxSupplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts.** The compressor's startup spike is the spec that most often trips small stations. Sources differ on its size: about 900-1,200 W for typical fridges ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)) and up to 2,400 W for large or older ones ([BlackBoxSupplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)). I'd look for 1,300 W or more, and more if your fridge is big or old. You also want pure sine wave output.
3. **Watt-hours.** The compressor only runs about a third of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70 W. One guide estimates ~1,400 Wh for a day and ~2,800 Wh for two, including inverter losses and headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

To get your own number, find the kWh/year on the fridge's yellow EnergyGuide label. Then multiply by 1,000 and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Multiply that by the outage hours, then add about 20-40% for losses and a margin. Hot kitchens, ice makers and frequent door openings push usage up.

## Picks that fit

Prices were checked Oct 21-24, 2026 and may change. These are affiliate links.

| Need | Model | Specs | Est. fridge runtime* | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| About 1.5 days (best value) | [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) | 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W, 3,900 W surge | ~34 hrs | $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF |
| Multi-day | [BLUETTI Elite 300](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-300) | 3,014 Wh, 2,400 W, 4,800 W surge | ~2 days | $1,199 (pre-order, ships from Oct 23) |
| Expandable later | [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) | 2,048 Wh, expandable to 8,192 Wh | ~33 hrs | $899, or $854.05 with AFF5OFF |
| Shorter outages | [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) | 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W surge | ~12-17 hrs | $499, or $474.05 with AFF5OFF |
| Budget | [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh) | 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W, 3,600 W peak | ~16 hrs | $439, or $395.10 with ALLPOWERS26 |

*Runtimes are HomeGridHQ's estimates for a 150 W fridge at a 35% duty cycle ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)). The ~12-17 hr figure for the AC180 is my estimate from its ~1,000 Wh class, not a listed number. Your results will vary.

Sources: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/how-much-power-does-a-household-refrigerator-use-watts-startup-surge-energy-per-), [HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator), [BlackBoxSupplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage).

Skip anything around 300 Wh or 600 W (such as the Elite 30 V2 or ALLPOWERS R600). Those can't handle a fridge for a full outage.

If you tell me your fridge's EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
